 7 weather alerts in effect First Alert Weather Day: Wind, heavy rain and snow could complicate Monday travel 
 Gusts of 60 to 65 mph are possible in parts of western South Dakota as fog, heavy rain and potential mountain snow affect KOTA Territory. 
 A Monday storm could bring 60-plus mph gusts to western South Dakota, heavy rain to Rapid City and snow to the Black Hills and northeastern Wyoming. By Ryan Hill Published : Nov. 1, 2026 at 7:40 PM CST | Updated : 7 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google RAPID CITY, S.D. (KOTA) - Damaging wind gusts, areas of dense fog, heavy rain and possible snow could create difficult travel conditions across parts of KOTA Territory on Monday.
 The First Alert Weather Team has declared Monday, Nov. 2, a First Alert Weather Day for the potential for wind gusts of 60 mph or higher in portions of western South Dakota. The strongest winds are expected near and east of the Black Hills, with gusts potentially reaching 65 mph in some locations.
 The storm also could bring more than an inch of rain to Rapid City, locally higher totals along the northern Black Hills slopes and parts of the western South Dakota plains, and accumulating snow in the higher elevations.
 Fog could complicate the morning drive
 Fog could again reduce visibility along portions of Interstate 90 and other roads in western South Dakota and northeastern Wyoming early Monday.
 Forecast guidance indicates the potential for sharply reduced visibility around 4 a.m., including near Wright, Wyoming; Ekalaka, Montana; and Philip, South Dakota. Some model projections show visibility falling to one-eighth of a mile near Wright, about half a mile near Philip and near zero around Ekalaka.
 Those figures are forecast possibilities, not observed conditions. Visibility could vary considerably over short distances, with especially difficult driving in pockets of dense fog.
 Heavy rain potential increases
 Rain could begin as early as midnight, with periods of heavier rainfall developing along and south of I-90 as Monday gets underway.
 Recent forecast guidance has shifted the better moisture farther west into western South Dakota, increasing the potential for substantial rainfall in and around Rapid City.
 Rapid City could receive roughly 1 to 1.75 inches of rain, with some guidance suggesting totals could approach 2 inches. More than 2 inches is possible along portions of the northern Black Hills slopes and on parts of the western South Dakota plains farther east.
 The placement of the heaviest rain remains uncertain and will depend on how the storm develops.
 Snow could reach lower elevations in northeastern Wyoming
 Colder air could allow rain to mix with or change to snow in portions of northeastern Wyoming, including around Gillette, Wright, Sundance and Sheridan. Slick spots are possible if temperatures fall enough, including in parts of Campbell County.
 In the Black Hills, the best chance for accumulating snow appears to be around 5,000 feet and higher, including terrain above Deadwood.
 Heavy precipitation could help cool the air and lower snow levels. An inch or two of snow is possible where temperatures become cold enough, though accumulation will depend on elevation, precipitation intensity and how quickly rain changes to snow.
 Forecast snowfall totals remain uncertain. Not every location that sees snow will receive accumulating snow.
 Strong winds could continue into Tuesday morning
 Communities identified in the high wind watch area include Spearfish, Rapid City, Belle Fourche, Newell, Nisland, Vale, Buffalo, Bison, Lemmon, Faith, Philip, Kadoka and Hot Springs, along with areas north of Pine Ridge toward Kyle. Parts of Butte County also are included.
 The strongest gusts are expected just east of the Black Hills and across portions of northwestern and west-central South Dakota, including the corridor from Buffalo toward Rapid City.
 Gusts could exceed 60 mph, with isolated gusts near 65 mph possible if stronger winds above the surface mix down. Forecast winds near 5,000 feet could reach about 70 mph Monday evening, but that does not mean those speeds will occur at ground level.
 Winds should begin easing toward 6 a.m. Tuesday, although gusts around 45 mph could linger.
 Residents should secure trash cans, outdoor furniture and remaining Halloween or fall decorations before winds increase. Strong gusts could cause damage, scatter debris and make travel especially difficult for tractor-trailers, pickups and SUVs.
 Stay away from downed power lines and fallen trees, and watch for debris on roads.
 Cooler Monday, followed by calmer weather
 Rapid City is forecast to fall to about 48 degrees Sunday night before reaching a high near 51 Monday. Philip could reach about 55 degrees.
 Colder conditions are expected in northeastern Wyoming and the Black Hills, where some locations could remain in the upper 30s or lower 40s.
 Conditions should become calmer later in the week, with highs generally returning to the upper 50s and lower 60s. A weak front could bring another round of gusty winds Saturday, potentially near 40 mph, before temperatures rebound toward the 60s Sunday.
 Follow the First Alert Weather Team on KOTA-TV and KEVN-TV and through KOTA Territory News for updates on rainfall, snow levels and wind timing.
